code: nul_terminated_data = (unsigned char *) g_strndup ((const gchar *) data, size);
note: The 1-byte attacker input 0xfd is copied into a 2-byte heap buffer (1 data byte + NUL terminator), allocated at [0x602000000070,0x602000000072).
The attacker-controlled string "\xfd" (invalid UTF-8) is passed to g_date_set_parse.
g_date_set_parse does NOT validate that str is valid UTF-8 before parsing; it forwards the raw bytes to g_date_prepare_to_parse.
The invalid UTF-8 string is forwarded to the token parser.
Since the input has no digits, pt->num_ints < 3, so the month-name matching branch runs and calls g_utf8_casefold on the invalid UTF-8 string with len=-1.
g_utf8_casefold iterates over the string and calls g_utf8_get_char on the byte 0xfd, which is not validated as UTF-8.
g_utf8_get_char reads the leading byte 0xfd; UTF8_COMPUTE classifies it as the start of a 5-byte UTF-8 sequence (len=5).
UTF8_GET reads 5 bytes starting at p, but the heap buffer only holds 1 data byte plus the NUL terminator, so it reads past the end of the 2-byte allocation -> heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1.
